source_refs.note: Book p. 228: 12.2.8 statement of the Sandwich Theorem and the two sentences leading into 12.2.9

blocks.text: Ab tak hum limits ko seedha value rakh kar, factor bana kar, ya upar neeche divide kar ke nikaalte aaye hain. Lekin kuch functions aise hote hain jin par yeh algebraic tareeqe kaam nahin karte. Aaj hum ek naya hathiyar seekhenge: Sandwich Theorem (isay Squeeze Theorem bhi kehte hain, yani "dabaane wala theorem").

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Idea bohat seedha hai: agar ek mushkil function ko do aasan functions ke beech phansa (trap) diya jaye, aur woh dono aasan functions ek hi jagah ja rahe hon, to beech wale function ke paas bhi wahin jane ke ilawa koi rasta nahin bachta.

Kitab ka theorem:
Let \(f\), \(g\) and \(h\) be functions such that \(f(x) \le g(x) \le h(x)\) for all numbers \(x\) in some open interval containing "\(c\)", except possibly at \(c\) itself.

If \(\lim_{x \to c} f(x) = L\) and \(\lim_{x \to c} h(x) = L\), then
\[\lim_{x \to c} g(x) = L\]

blocks.title: Teaching note

blocks.text:
Kitab aage likhti hai ke bohat se limit ke sawal aise hote hain jo algebraic tareeqon se seedhe hal nahin hote; un ke liye geometry (shakal) ki daleel chahiye hoti hai. Is liye ab hum ek ahem theorem saabit karenge.
Yeh ishara agle heading 12.2.9 ki taraf hai, jahan \(\lim_{\theta \to 0}\frac{\sin\theta}{\theta} = 1\) ko circle ki ek figure aur isi Sandwich Theorem se saabit kiya jayega.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin: \(\lim_{x \to 0} x^{2}\sin\frac{1}{x}\) nikaaliye.
Masla: \(x = 0\) rakh nahin sakte, kyun ke \(\frac{1}{0}\) ka matlab nahin, aur \(\sin\frac{1}{x}\) zero ke qareeb bohat tezi se \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech jhoolta rehta hai. Is ki apni koi limit nahin.
Hal: hum jaante hain ke sine ki value hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech hoti hai: \(-1 \le \sin\frac{1}{x} \le 1\). Ab poori inequality ko \(x^{2}\) se zarb dein; \(x^{2}\) positive hai, is liye nishaan nahin badalte:
\[-x^{2} \le x^{2}\sin\dfrac{1}{x} \le x^{2}\]
Neeche wali roti \(-x^{2} \to 0\) aur oopar wali roti \(x^{2} \to 0\) jab \(x \to 0\). Dono ek hi jagah (0) ja rahi hain, to Sandwich Theorem se jawab 0 hai.
Khud sochiye: \(\lim_{x \to 0} x\cos\frac{1}{x}\) kya hoga? (Ishara: \(-|x| \le x\cos\frac{1}{x} \le |x|\); jawab 0.)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(f(x) \le g(x) \le h(x)\) (\(c\) ke qareeb), aur \(f, h\) dono ki limit \(L\) ho, to \(g\) ki limit bhi \(L\).
2. Dono bahar wali (outer) limits barabar honi chahiye.
3. Inequality sirf \(c\) ke aas paas chahiye, \(c\) par nahin.
4. Jab algebra kaam na kare, khaas taur par \(\sin\) aur \(\cos\) wale functions mein (jo hamesha \(-1\) aur \(1\) ke beech rehte hain), yeh theorem yaad kijiye.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Do aisi hadein (bounds) lena jin ki limits alag alag hon, jaise \(0 \le g(x) \le 1\). Is se sirf itna pata chalta hai ke limit (agar ho) 0 aur 1 ke beech hai; limit nahin milti.
2. Inequality ko negative number se zarb dena aur nishaan na palatna. Negative se zarb dein to \(\le\) ulta ho kar \(\ge\) ban jata hai.
3. \(\lim x^{2}\sin\frac{1}{x}\) ko \(\lim x^{2} \cdot \lim\sin\frac{1}{x}\) likh dena. Product wala theorem tabhi lagta hai jab dono limits maujood hon; \(\sin\frac{1}{x}\) ki limit maujood hi nahin, isi liye Sandwich chahiye.
